newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes see La. sweets continue drive higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes see La. sweets continue drive higher.

text.p: U.S. crudes gained strength Monday morning, posting stronger differentials for key sweet grades on concerns over North Sea supply disruptions.

Cash traders said a protest blockade at main U.K. export terminal Sullom Voe raised the price for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James a few cents. Local fisherman are protesting delays in compensatory payments following the Braer tanker spill in 1993.
Despite the fisherman's efforts, Sullom Voe loading operations proceeded as normal.

Underlying support for LLS/St. James continued from the stronger Brent market, where paper spreads have moved into backwardation. North Sea and West African supplies have been siphoned to Far East destinations in recent days, slowing the transport of foreign crudes to the U.S. Gulf.
Outright June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing rallied a sharp 75 cents to $21.15-25 a barrel, and hung firm against July with a 10-12 cents premium building by late morning.

NYMEX futures have pegged the rally on technical buying and fears of heightened Middle East tensions. Iran launched a new set of wargames in the hyper-sensitive Strait of Hormuz, where the brunt of Middle East oil transits for export.
Iran is the world's third largest oil producer.
For the grades, LLS/St. James was sold between 9-11 cents over the June WTI/Cushing, 2-4 cents stronger than Friday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire talked at a steady 35-25 cents discount, and Midland/WTI went unchallenged at 31-28 cts below the benchmark.
West Texas Sour/Midland was also steady at $1.50-1.43 under WTI, and Eugene Island came in steady this morning too, at ranges between $1.45-35 cheaper than the marker.
